info.title: Anupalan API
info.summary: Compliance engine for packaged commodities in India
info.description: Advisory pre-audit tool. Output is not a certification and carries no legal force. The rule pack is an engineering transcription pending legal review.

get.description:
Report process health plus the state of each dependency and the active rule pack.

``rulepack`` is read from the loaded pack's ``meta`` (never hardcoded), so this endpoint
doubles as proof that the pack on disk parsed and is the version you expect.

post.description:
Send a code to a phone number.

Answers identically whether or not the number is registered (see the module docstring), so a
caller learns nothing from this endpoint except that their request was accepted.

Verify a code and start a session.

The code is consumed whether or not it turns out to belong to a registered number, so a
caller cannot use a valid-but-unregistered code twice to probe for a race.

Exchange a refresh token for a new pair.

Rotation: the presented token is retired and a new one issued in the same family. Presenting a
retired token revokes the whole family — see the module docstring for why that is the right
response to an ambiguous signal.

get.description:
Who the bearer token says you are.

Useful to the app on cold start, and useful in testing as the smallest endpoint that proves
the whole token path works. It returns no new tokens — the ones in the response are the empty
strings, because the caller already holds the only one that matters.

post.summary: Create a scan and get upload URLs
post.description:
Create a scan and issue one presigned upload URL per asset (FR-20).

The API never sees the image. It records what the client says it is about to upload — content
type, size and SHA-256 — signs a URL for each, and leaves. The size and type are enforced
*here*, when the capability is issued, rather than after the bytes have arrived.

get.description:
A page of this org's scans, newest first (FR-09).

*Accept: filtering 200 seeded scans by ``verdict=FAIL`` returns only scans with at least one
FAIL, within 500 ms.*

The shape that makes the second half of that true: **filter, page, then aggregate**. The verdict
filter is an ``IN`` against a grouped sub-select rather than a count computed per row, the page
is a keyset slice of at most a hundred scans, and only those scans' findings are counted. Adding
scans to an org lengthens the table, not the work.

parameters.name: verdict

schema.description: Scans having at least one finding with this verdict, in their current evaluation. **Exactly one verdict, never a set.** Widening this to mean 'has a problem' by including BORDERLINE alongside FAIL would collapse the two (CLAUDE.md §3.4) and would not look like a bug: the list would be longer and every scan in it would genuinely have something on it. What it destroys is the distinction the product exists for — an inspector asking for failures would be shown a compliant pack whose measurement merely sat inside the uncertainty band.
schema.title: Verdict

parameters.description: Scans having at least one finding with this verdict, in their current evaluation. **Exactly one verdict, never a set.** Widening this to mean 'has a problem' by including BORDERLINE alongside FAIL would collapse the two (CLAUDE.md §3.4) and would not look like a bug: the list would be longer and every scan in it would genuinely have something on it. What it destroys is the distinction the product exists for — an inspector asking for failures would be shown a compliant pack whose measurement merely sat inside the uncertainty band.

parameters.name: tz_offset_minutes

schema.description: Minutes the caller's clock is ahead of UTC, so `from` and `to` mean the caller's calendar days. Defaults to UTC days.
schema.title: Tz Offset Minutes

parameters.description: Minutes the caller's clock is ahead of UTC, so `from` and `to` mean the caller's calendar days. Defaults to UTC days.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: Free text over the product name
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Free text over the product name

post.description:
Enqueue processing and return immediately (FR-20: 202 inside 300 ms).

This handler does not open an image, call OCR, or touch object storage. It flips a status and
puts a message on a queue — which is the only way the latency budget is achievable, and the
reason the pipeline is a Celery task rather than a background coroutine.

Idempotent without needing a key: a scan already queued or further along is returned as it
stands rather than enqueued twice.

get.summary: Fetch a scan and its assets
get.description:
A scan, its status and its assets with time-limited read URLs.

Buckets are private (architecture §10), so a presigned GET is the only read path. The URLs are
minted per request and expire; nothing here hands out a durable link to evidence.

get.summary: The verdicts that stand for a scan
get.description:
The current findings — the highest evaluation revision's (FR-05).

Always carries ``rulepack_version`` (CLAUDE.md §3.6) and the summary block, including the
count of rules that did not apply.

**An empty findings list is a real answer, not an error.** A scan in ``needs_confirmation``
has been read and deliberately not judged: its extractions, measurements and OCR are all here,
and there are no verdicts because ``evaluate()`` was never run over a value nobody has checked.
The response still carries the pack version the confirmation will be judged under, so a client
can say *which* rules are waiting rather than only that something is. The 409 below is
therefore about a scan that has not been *processed* — no evaluation row at all — which is a
different statement and the one it was always meant to make.

post.summary: Correct extracted fields and recompute the verdict
post.description:
Record human corrections and re-evaluate (FR-06).

The recompute runs against **the pack the scan was originally evaluated under and the original
``as_of``** — not the active pack, and not today's date. A report regenerated next year must
reproduce the verdict issued under the rules in force at scan time (CLAUDE.md §3.6), and a
correction is not a reason to re-judge a label against rules that did not exist when it was
photographed.

Nothing is mutated. The superseded extraction keeps its row, the previous findings keep
theirs, and the result is a new evaluation revision.

get.description:
Walk the chain and report the first link that does not hold.

Org-scoped like everything else: an admin verifies their own authority's record, not anyone
else's. Each org has its own chain, starting from a genesis hash, so one tenant's activity
neither reveals nor depends on another's.

Entries in chain order, oldest first — the only order that means anything for a linked
list, and the order verification walks.

get.summary: Verdict counts grouped by one dimension
get.description:
Violations for this org, grouped and counted by the database.

The window is on ``captured_at``, the date the photograph was taken, because that is the date
the inspection happened. FR-04 lets a scan sit in an offline queue for days, so filtering on
when the row arrived would move inspections into months in which they did not occur.

parameters.name: group_by

schema.description: Which axis to group on. Anything outside this enum is a 422.

parameters.description: Which axis to group on. Anything outside this enum is a 422.

schema.description: Earliest capture date, inclusive (not upload date)

post.summary: Ask Sahayak a BIS certification question
post.description:
Retrieve, generate with mandatory citation, post-validate, and record.

The question is passed to retrieval **as asked**, and that has not changed: rewriting what the
user asked before searching makes the answer depend on a rewrite nobody can see. A ``scan_id``
is still not folded into the question text.

What a ``scan_id`` now does add is **grounding for the generation**: the scan's frozen profile
is rendered into the prompt so an answer about "this product" knows what the product is,
instead of the model inferring it from whatever the question happened to spell out. The two
stages are deliberately separate — retrieval stays reproducible from the question alone, and
the product can steer the wording of an answer without steering which sources it may cite.

It grants the product no authority. ``services/bis/answer`` requires every claim to name a
retrieved passage, so a certification requirement can still only come from published material;
the lookup at ``/bis/applicability`` remains the only thing that decides applicability.

post.summary: Does a BIS Quality Control Order cover this product?
post.description:
Look the product up against the published QCO and CRS lists (FR-29).

A table lookup, deterministic and reproducible. No model is called and no retrieval happens:
the answer is whatever the reviewed list in ``bis/`` says, stamped with the list's version and
the row that decided it, so it can be checked against the published source.

post.summary: BIS applicability for a scanned product
post.description:
The same lookup, against the profile the scan was **frozen** with (FR-29).

This is the join between the two problem statements: the profile that decided which Legal
Metrology declarations applied also decides the certification route. Read from the scan's own
frozen copy rather than from ``products``, for the reason ``models/scan.py`` gives — a product
edited next month must not change an answer already given about a package photographed today.

post.summary: Check a CSV of marketplace listings (Mode B)
post.description:
Run presence and format rules over every listing in the CSV (FR-10).

Gated on ``PRODUCT_READ`` rather than ``PRODUCT_WRITE``: the check persists nothing, creates
nothing, and reads only text the caller supplied in the request body. Requiring the write
permission would lock the flagship Mode B feature away from the analyst role that exists to
run it, for a call that leaves no trace.

``as_of`` is today. Unlike a scan — which is judged at its capture date, because FR-04 lets a
photograph sit in an offline queue for days — a pasted listing has no capture date. It is a
live listing being checked now, so now is the honest date to judge it at.

get.summary: List and search the product catalogue
get.description:
This org's products, alphabetically (FR-03, FR-09).

Alphabetical rather than newest-first because the caller is a person looking for a product they
already have in mind, in a picker. Recency is the right order for a history of events and the
wrong one for a catalogue.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: Free text over name and brand
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Free text over name and brand

post.summary: Generate a report for a scan
post.description:
Render this scan's current findings and store them (FR-27, FR-08).

Refuses a scan that has never been evaluated. There is nothing to report on, and a document
stating no findings would read as a clean result rather than as an absent one.

get.description:
One report, with fresh read URLs.

The links are minted per request and expire, so this is also how a client re-shares a report it
generated yesterday — nothing hands out a durable link to evidence.

post.summary: Read a pack's photographs to prefill the product context form
post.description:
Accept a pack's photographs and queue them to be read (FR-03).

Returns immediately with an id to poll. The read happens in the worker, which is where the OCR
models live — the API process does not load them and must not start doing so on a request
path.

Permissioned as ``SCAN_CREATE``: prefill is part of creating a scan, and anyone who may not
create one has no use for a form to be filled.

get.summary: Collect what a pack's photographs suggest for the context form
get.description:
Return one prefill, or 404 once it has expired.

``no-store`` because the answer changes from ``reading`` to ``ready`` within seconds and a
cached ``reading`` is a form that never fills.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How well the cited sources matched the question — a retrieval signal, not a probability that the answer is correct. Null when no reranker ran.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Freshness of the material behind this answer

ApplicabilityIn.title: ApplicabilityIn
ApplicabilityIn.description: A product profile to look up.

matched_entry_id.title: Matched Entry Id
matched_entry_id.description: The list row that decided it. Null when nothing matched.

order.title: Order
order.description: The Quality Control Order, where named

forthcoming.title: Forthcoming
forthcoming.description: Obligations that match this product but are not yet in force

ApplicabilityOut.title: ApplicabilityOut
ApplicabilityOut.description: FR-29's shape, plus the provenance that makes it checkable.

scan_id.title: Scan Id
scan_id.description: Link the question to a scan of this org. Recorded on the query so a certification answer a brand acted on can be shown next to the label it was asked about.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: Checked against the allow-list when the URL is signed, and part of the signature, so the uploaded bytes must match it

size_bytes.title: Size Bytes
size_bytes.description: Enforced at presign time, not after the upload

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes about to be uploaded. The worker verifies the stored object against this before processing; a mismatch fails the scan.

AssetIn.title: AssetIn
AssetIn.description: One image the client is about to upload.

url.title: Url
url.description: Time-limited read URL. Buckets are private; this is the only read path.

BBoxOut.title: BBoxOut
BBoxOut.description: Evidence rectangle on the rectified image, in pixels (FR-05: tappable).

borderline.title: Borderline
borderline.description: BORDERLINE — within the measurement's uncertainty band, never a failure

not_assessable.title: Not Assessable
not_assessable.description: NOT_ASSESSABLE — could not be checked, e.g. no marker, so no millimetres

scans.title: Scans
scans.description: Distinct scans contributing to this group

key.title: Key
key.description: The group's value. **null** means the dimension was not recorded on those scans — an unknown district, or a scan with no product to take a brand from — and never that the group is empty.

BucketOut.title: BucketOut
BucketOut.description:
One row of the dashboard table: a group and its counts, flat.

Flat rather than ``{key, counts:{...}}`` because a bucket *is* a table row, and every consumer
— a chart, a CSV export, a sorted list — wants the columns at one level.

csv.title: Csv
csv.description: CSV text. Needs a header with a listing text column — one of `listing_text`, `text`, `description`, `listing` — plus optional `listing_id`/`sku`, `url`, and any profile columns (`is_imported`, `category_code`, `net_qty_value`, ...).

profile.description: Defaults for rows that do not carry their own profile columns.

BulkListingIn.title: BulkListingIn
BulkListingIn.description:
A pasted CSV of marketplace listings (FR-10).

A single text field rather than a multipart upload: "paste or upload" are the same payload
once the client has read the file, and one content type is one thing to get right in the
generated mobile client.

rulepack_version.title: Rulepack Version
rulepack_version.description: Every verdict here was issued under this pack (CLAUDE.md §3.6)

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: A listing carries no physical scale, so every metric and geometry rule in every row is NOT_ASSESSABLE. Stated on the response so a client cannot render these verdicts as though they came from a measured photograph.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: broken_link: a row was deleted or inserted. hash_mismatch: a row's contents were edited.

ChainBreakOut.title: ChainBreakOut
ChainBreakOut.description: One place the chain stopped verifying.

first_break.description: Where the chain stops being provable. Null when it is intact.

ChainVerificationOut.title: ChainVerificationOut
ChainVerificationOut.description: The result of walking this org's chain.

section.title: Section
section.description: Where in the document — a clause, not a page number

ConfirmFieldsIn.title: ConfirmFieldsIn
ConfirmFieldsIn.description: Confirm or correct low-confidence fields and recompute the verdict.

borderline.title: Borderline
borderline.description: BORDERLINE — within the measurement's uncertainty band, never a failure

not_assessable.title: Not Assessable
not_assessable.description: NOT_ASSESSABLE — could not be checked, e.g. no marker, so no millimetres

scans.title: Scans
scans.description: Distinct scans contributing to this group

CountsOut.title: CountsOut
CountsOut.description:
The four verdicts for one group, with its row and scan counts.

``pass`` is a Python keyword, so the field is ``passed`` and the wire name is set by an alias.
The wire name is the contract ``mobile/`` generates against and matches the summary block of
``GET /v1/scans/{id}/findings``; renaming it to dodge the keyword would leave one system with
two spellings of the same four verdicts.

value_raw.title: Value Raw
value_raw.description: Exactly as it appeared on the pack

value_norm.title: Value Norm
value_norm.description: Units resolved, dates parsed. Null when normalisation failed.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The extractor's own confidence. The client confirms anything below its threshold before treating a verdict as settled, so this must be the real number — a default of 1.0 on an uncertain read disables FR-06 silently.

source_span.title: Source Span
source_span.description: Character range in the OCR text this value came from, verified to exist in that text before the value was accepted (CLAUDE.md §8).

ExtractionOut.title: ExtractionOut
ExtractionOut.description:
One extracted declaration, as it currently stands (FR-24, FR-06).

Superseded rows are absent: a human correction writes a new row and stamps the old one, so this
is the set the verdicts were computed from and the set the client should show.

code.title: Code
code.description: One of the 15 field codes of FR-24

value.title: Value
value.description: What the label actually says. Recorded as value_raw with source=human, so format rules see exactly what the person read off the pack.

FieldCorrectionIn.title: FieldCorrectionIn
FieldCorrectionIn.description: One human correction to an extracted declaration (FR-06).

finding_id.title: Finding Id
finding_id.description: The stored row. Stable within an evaluation revision and replaced wholesale by the next one, because a recompute writes new rows rather than mutating these. **Null when the finding was computed rather than stored** — the bulk listing check (FR-10) judges text that was never a scan, so there is no evidence row to point at, and that is the same reason such a finding can never be corrected or reported on.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The sub-rule, verbatim from the pack

band.title: Band
band.description: The uncertainty band printed on a BORDERLINE verdict, e.g. 1.80-2.30. Printing it is what stops a borderline reading being read as an accusation.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Which evaluation these findings come from. 0 is the pipeline's; each confirm-fields recompute increments it, and the old rows survive.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The date effective-date filtering was done against — the capture date, never the current clock.

reduced_extraction.title: Reduced Extraction
reduced_extraction.description: True when the LLM layer did not run or did not answer, so the extraction was regex-only (architecture §11).

findings_sha256.title: Findings Sha256
findings_sha256.description: The digest stored with this evaluation, over the canonical findings JSON. A report embeds the same value (architecture §10), so the two surfaces agree by construction rather than by two code paths happening to match.

extractions.title: Extractions
extractions.description: Current extracted declarations. Drives FR-06's confirmation sheet and gates report generation — see this module's docstring for why it is never omitted.

na.title: Na
na.description: NOT_ASSESSABLE — could not be checked from this image

not_applicable.title: Not Applicable
not_applicable.description: Rules that did not apply to this product — not a verdict

GeoOut.title: GeoOut
GeoOut.description:
Where a Mode A inspection happened.

Nested rather than three flat columns, because it is one fact: a reading with a latitude and no
accuracy is not a usable position, and a client that had to assemble it from three nullable
fields would have to decide what a partial one means. Null for every Mode B scan — industry
users are never asked for a location (architecture §10).

status.title: Status
status.description: ok only when every component is ok

rulepack.title: Rulepack
rulepack.description: Active rule pack as CODE-vVERSION, read from the pack's meta block

row_number.title: Row Number
row_number.description: 1-based line in the uploaded file, header included — what a spreadsheet shows

url.title: Url
url.description: Recorded as provenance and never fetched. An endpoint that requested caller-supplied URLs would be a server-side request forgery with a CSV interface.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why this row could not be checked. Null when it was.

glyph.title: Glyph
glyph.description: The glyph measured, where a rule is about one

uncertainty_mm.title: Uncertainty Mm
uncertainty_mm.description: Half-width of the uncertainty band. A reading within this of a threshold is BORDERLINE. Null means it could not be established — never read a null as zero, which would be a claim of perfect measurement.

method.title: Method
method.description: How it was obtained. Glyph heights come from connected components on the rectified image, never from OCR polygons, which include ascenders and padding.

MeasurementOut.title: MeasurementOut
MeasurementOut.description:
One physical measurement behind a metric verdict (FR-23).

Empty for a scan with no marker — that is the whole of CLAUDE.md §3.3 expressed as data, and it
is what makes every metric rule NOT_ASSESSABLE rather than a guess.

OrgOut.title: OrgOut
OrgOut.description: The org a session belongs to.

code.title: Code
code.description: The code itself, returned only in non-production environments with OTP_ECHO_IN_RESPONSE on, where no SMS gateway is configured. Never populated in production.

OtpRequestOut.title: OtpRequestOut
OtpRequestOut.description:
The handle for the code that was just sent.

Deliberately identical whether or not the number belongs to a user. A response that differed
would let anyone test whether a phone number has an account here — which, for an enforcement
deployment, means testing whether someone is an inspector.

PrefillAcceptedOut.title: PrefillAcceptedOut
PrefillAcceptedOut.description: The read has been queued. Poll ``GET /v1/prefill/{prefill_id}``.

images.title: Images
images.description: In capture order, at most MAX_PREFILL_IMAGES. A client holding more sends the first three rather than the whole capture — later photographs are usually another angle on a face already read, and each one costs an OCR pass on a wait somebody is watching.

PrefillCreateIn.title: PrefillCreateIn
PrefillCreateIn.description:
The photographs of one pack, to be read together for the context form.

**Not just the front panel.** A pack's mandatory declarations are spread across its faces: the
net quantity and the commodity name are usually on the front, the importer, the country of
origin and the consumer-care line usually on the back. Reading one photograph proposes nothing
for most of the fields a user would otherwise type, so the client sends the photographs it has
and the worker merges their words before extracting once.

**Up to three of them.** See ``MAX_PREFILL_IMAGES`` for why three and not the scan's asset
limit.

image_base64.title: Image Base64
image_base64.description: The photograph, base64-encoded, downscaled by the client. The decoded size is checked against PREFILL_MAX_BYTES across the whole request; this per-image length cap is the cheap first refusal so a very large body is rejected before it is decoded.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: Media type of the encoded bytes. Decides the scratch object's extension only — recognition reads the bytes, not this.

word_count.title: Word Count
word_count.description: Words recognised across every photograph. Zero with no suggestions means they were read and had nothing usable on them, which is a different thing from the read failing.

reduced.title: Reduced
reduced.description: True when extraction ran pattern-only. No pattern reads a common name, so a reduced read will not propose a product name.

ProductOut.title: ProductOut
ProductOut.description:
One catalogue entry.

Flat rather than a nested profile, and the flatness is the honest shape. A scan's ``profile`` is
a complete set of answers because FR-03 makes the operator supply the missing ones; a catalogue
row is whatever has been recorded about a product so far. Nesting it would imply the two are
interchangeable and would need this endpoint to invent the fields a catalogue does not hold.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Opaque — see routers/pagination.py. Null on the last page.

ProductPageOut.title: ProductPageOut
ProductPageOut.description: A page of catalogue entries, alphabetical.

net_qty_in_g_or_ml.title: Net Qty In G Or Ml
net_qty_in_g_or_ml.description: Net quantity normalised to g or ml — the Table-I key

pdp_area_cm2.title: Pdp Area Cm2
pdp_area_cm2.description: Principal display panel area — the Table-II key

ProfileIn.title: ProfileIn
ProfileIn.description:
The product context that decides which rules apply (FR-03).

Mirrors ``services.rules.types.Profile``. Field names are part of the rule pack's contract —
packs address them as ``profile.is_imported``, ``profile.net_qty_in_g_or_ml`` — so renaming
one here breaks a pack, not just a client.

net_qty_in_g_or_ml.title: Net Qty In G Or Ml

ProfileOut.title: ProfileOut
ProfileOut.description:
The product context a scan was judged under.

Mirrors ``ProfileIn`` but does **not** inherit ``StrictModel``. This is deliberate and the
direction matters: a request with an unknown field is a client bug worth a 422, while a *stored*
profile carrying a key this version does not know is our own older data, and refusing to render
it would turn a schema addition into a 500 on every scan recorded before it. Unknown keys are
dropped from the response; the rule pack reads the stored JSON directly, so no verdict
depends on what this model chooses to show.

RefreshIn.title: RefreshIn
RefreshIn.description: Present a refresh token for rotation.

formats.title: Formats
formats.description: At least one. Duplicates are collapsed; order does not matter.

url.title: Url
url.description: Time-limited read URL. Buckets are private (architecture §10), so this is the only read path and it expires — fetch the bytes, do not store the link.

evaluation_id.title: Evaluation Id
evaluation_id.description: Which evaluation this report states. A later correction makes a new revision and does not change what this document said.

status.title: Status
status.description: ``ready`` as soon as it exists. ``pending`` is reserved for the asynchronous form — see this module's docstring — so a polling client is correct either way.

formats.title: Formats
formats.description: What was asked for. Kept beside ``files`` on purpose: a report delivering one of two requested documents must be visible as a short delivery rather than reading as though only one was ever wanted.

image_sha256.title: Image Sha256
image_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw image as received. Null when the scan has no raw asset — which the client shows as an unverifiable image rather than as a verified one.

marker_type.title: Marker Type
marker_type.description: FR-02: the scale reference in frame

marker_mm.title: Marker Mm
marker_mm.description: Declared physical size of the marker. Per-scan, never a constant: a 40 mm tag and an ID-1 card are both valid and are different numbers.

captured_at.title: Captured At
captured_at.description: When the photograph was taken. This is the evaluator's as_of, so an offline capture uploaded a week later is still judged against the rules in force when it was taken (FR-04). Defaults to now.

district.title: District
district.description: Revenue district the inspection happened in — FR-30's Mode A dashboard axis. Recorded from the client, never derived from the coordinates above: resolving a point to a district would be a guess made by a boundary file of unknown vintage, and Mode B sends no coordinates at all, so half the rows could not be resolved even in principle. Null is the correct value for every Mode B scan.

ScanCreateIn.title: ScanCreateIn
ScanCreateIn.description: Create a scan and ask for upload URLs.

ScanCreatedOut.title: ScanCreatedOut
ScanCreatedOut.description:
What ``POST /v1/scans`` returns.

Replayed verbatim for a retried ``Idempotency-Key``, presigned URLs included — a retry must
get back what it got the first time rather than a fresh set of credentials.

product_id.title: Product Id
product_id.description: Null for a scan whose profile was typed in and never matched to a catalogue product. An id rather than a name, because two products can share a name and a filter matching on text would quietly fold them together.

product_name.title: Product Name
product_name.description: The catalogue product's name if the scan is linked to one, otherwise the name declared on the scan's own profile. Null when neither exists — which the client shows as an unnamed scan rather than inventing a label for it.

thumbnail_url.title: Thumbnail Url
thumbnail_url.description: Time-limited read URL for the annotated image, falling back to the rectified and then the raw one. Null when the scan has no image yet or object storage is unreachable — a list of scans is still readable without its pictures.

ScanListItemOut.title: ScanListItemOut
ScanListItemOut.description:
One row of the history list (FR-09).

Compact on purpose: the list renders hundreds of these, so it carries counts rather than
findings and one thumbnail rather than every asset.

org_id.title: Org Id
org_id.description: The owning tenant. Returned so a client can assert it is showing what it thinks it is; it is never accepted on the way in (see schemas/base.py).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Who recorded the scan. Null for one created before users existed.

profile.description: The context that decided which rules applied. On the scan rather than fetched separately, because a product's catalogue entry can change after a scan and the verdicts stand against what was declared at capture.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Opaque. Pass it back as ``cursor`` for the next page; null means this was the last one. Do not parse it — see routers/pagination.py.

ScanSubmittedOut.title: ScanSubmittedOut
ScanSubmittedOut.description:
The 202 from ``POST /v1/scans/{id}/submit``.

Deliberately thin. The endpoint enqueues and returns inside 300 ms (FR-20) and does not touch
an image, so there is nothing more it could truthfully say.

SessionOut.title: SessionOut
SessionOut.description: Everything the app needs after a successful sign-in.

SourceOut.title: SourceOut
SourceOut.description:
An official page to read. Offered on a refusal, where there is no citation but there is
still somewhere useful to send the reader.

field.title: Field
field.description: A profile field name: name, net_qty_value, net_qty_unit or is_imported. Never surface, pack_type, pdp_area_cm2, channel or category_code — see services/extraction/prefill.NEVER_SUGGESTED for why each is excluded.

value.title: Value
value.description: Always a string, including for is_imported ('true').

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: Inherited unchanged from the declaration this was read from. Below FR-06's 0.75 the machine does not believe its own reading, and the client says so.

from_field_code.title: From Field Code
from_field_code.description: The declaration the value was read from.

SuggestionOut.title: SuggestionOut
SuggestionOut.description:
One proposed product-context value, with the reading it came from.

``source_text`` and ``from_field_code`` are not decoration. A filled form field that cannot
say where its value came from asks the user to trust it; one that can says "this is what I
read on the pack, check it", which is the only version of this feature that is safe to ship
(CLAUDE.md §3.1).

TokenPairOut.title: TokenPairOut
TokenPairOut.description:
A new access token and the refresh token that will replace it.

The refresh token is rotated on every use, so the value here is always new — a client that
keeps the old one will invalidate its whole family the next time it tries to use it.

UploadOut.title: UploadOut
UploadOut.description: A capability to upload exactly one object.

VerdictCountsOut.title: VerdictCountsOut
VerdictCountsOut.description:
The four verdict counts for one scan in a list (FR-09).

Deliberately **not** ``FindingsSummary``, which carries a fifth count for rules that did not
apply. That fifth number needs the rule pack loaded to work out which rules were never reached,
which is a sensible cost once for one scan's findings screen and an absurd one for every row of
a two-hundred-row list. Four verdicts, four numbers, no pack.

All four are always present, zeroes included. A row that showed only its non-zero counts would
teach a reader that the counts shown are the only ones there are.

ViolationDimension.title: ViolationDimension
ViolationDimension.description:
The axes FR-30 names. Anything not in here is not a dimension.

``MONTH`` is "over time"; ``DISTRICT`` is Mode A's axis and ``BRAND`` is Mode B's. Both of
those read a column that is recorded rather than derived — see migration 0003 for why a
district resolved from coordinates would have been worse than no district at all.

rulepack_versions.title: Rulepack Versions
rulepack_versions.description: Every rule pack version represented in the window (CLAUDE.md §3.6). A percentage that cannot name the rules behind it cannot be reproduced.
